pr_title: timedated: Respond on org.freedesktop.timedate1.SetNTP only when real…
pr_body:
…ly finished

The method returns prematurely (before jobs it triggers terminate). This is externally visible because other methods may fail if jobs did not finish.
Postpone the DBus method response until we collect all signals for finished jobs.
In order not to maintains a list of all pending clients, we only implement this for the last calling client if multiple requests overlap.

Fixes: #17739

WDYT, @yuwata? (Only build-tested!)
pr_comments:
this makes a ton of sense to me, but please keep track of all message calls, as commented above..

Moving to the end looks more streamlined at it resolved my concerns, good idea.

issue_context.title: org.freedesktop.timedate1.SetNTP is not atomic, prevents other calls
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > …

246

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released (non-rc) systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd/releases for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > …
Any

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > …
5.9.2-arch1-1, but it will affect an

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > …
x86_64, but it will affect any

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 >
We call SetNtp() wait for it to finish, Call SetTime. Expectation is this succeeds correctly,

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 We call SetNtp() wait for it to finish, Call SetTime. 

"Failed to set current time "org.freedesktop.timedate1.AutomaticTimeSyncEnabled" "Previous request is not finished, refusing."

> Steps to reproduce:

One needs a binary that calls SetNtp() SetTime() consecutively, which is a sensible pattern for a GUI with an apply button.

Raised as downstream bug(https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=429112) 

> Code wise the issue is:

set_ntp does starts an async call and then returns success from the setNTP method
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/a2e926a135e0a88e5df3731e7fd682aba789cce9/src/timedate/timedated.c#L969

ntp property doesn't change until the "Job removed" signal comes in from systemd, via: match_job_removed
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/a2e926a135e0a88e5df3731e7fd682aba789cce9/src/timedate/timedated.c#L462

The set_time method fails if an existing job is still running:
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/a2e926a135e0a88e5df3731e7fd682aba789cce9/src/timedate/timedated.c#L812


General convention is that DBus methods only return when the property is actually updated.

Creating the call and then watching the property instead of the method returning will probably work as a downstream workaround, but it's messy as I can't correctly detect failures.

Alternatively returning the path to the systemd job in setNTP would work allow a much cleaner downstream patch.

review_comments:
this isn't really necessary btw. the bus broker puts a limit on in flight method calls anyway for each client, hence there's no real need to limits this here a second time.

This is a limit on "server" side. It is meant to avoid exhaustion in timedated context caused by (multiple) client processes.
Should timedated capacity be also considered indirectly limited by dbus capacity?

hmm, this will cause this method to return EAGAIN, which is a bit icky, since that is typically a local transient error, that suggests "retry later" locally. But from our pov this is not like that though, when we let the call fail here, we let it fail for good.

moreover sd_bus_error_set_errnof() is not a function you really should be using unless you actually received an error number from somewhere else. otherwise just return a proper dbus error.

hence, I'd either drop this (because broker already enforces a limit here), or make it return a proper dbus error.
